NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 23 : Stock indexes were mixed on Friday, with tech shares edging higher after the previous day's selloff, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest in more than five months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. The Nasdaq was up 0.2 per cent after starting the day lower, while the Dow was last down about 1 per cent. An index of semiconductors was up about 1 per cent. It posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June on Thursday after a report from Meta Platforms reignited worries about the AI trade. It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston.

"After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," he said. "But also, we continue to be in a place where things look like they're getting worse, not better, in the Middle East. That moves energy prices higher, which is obviously going to end up being a significant headwind for economic activity." Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned fears over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill. US crude rose 2.56 per cent to $102.02 a barrel and Brent climbed to $116.27 per barrel, up 2.74 per cent. European natural gas prices jumped.  AMEX, TELECOM SHARES FALL Investors were digesting corporate earnings news. American Express shares fell 3.5 per cent after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization. Telecom company shares, including Verizon, dropped after a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9 per cent, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 eased 11.14 points, or 0.14 per cent, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21 per cent, to 26,062.75. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 1.64 points, or 0.15 per cent, to 1,121.29.The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4 per cent. Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4 per cent earlier. US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5 per cent. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992 per cent. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since June. EURO FALLS The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances. French yields, which were down 5 basis points at 5.04 per cent, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May.  A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011. France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody’s later on Friday. The euro was last down 0.12 per cent at $1.12, set to end the week 0.35 per cent lower.

Source: Reuters

Oct 23 : US telecom stocks declined on Friday after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier, fueling concerns over fresh competition. Elon Musk's rocket and space technology company was in talks to access at least 80,000 cell sites to build its wireless carrier from scratch, Bloomberg News reported late on Thursday, citing sources familiar with the matter. AT&T fell 5.6 per cent to a more than three-month low, Verizon lost 1.6 per cent and T-Mobile shed 5 per cent.  Germany's Deutsche Telekom, which holds an over 50 per cent stake in T-Mobile, lost 3.2 per cent.

"The competitive impact may still be years away, but anticipation alone, reinforced by each successive spectrum and infrastructure move, is likely to remain an overhang on sector sentiment," Bernstein analysts said in a note. Tower operators and SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The report comes weeks after SpaceX acquired low-band spectrum to advance its carrier plans, mounting a direct, orbital challenge to legacy wireless giants in the US and sending AT&T and Verizon shares to their worst one-day falls in more than two decades. Bernstein analysts said that an MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) deal with SpaceX may not appeal to telecom operators, but a unified stance against one has done little to lift sentiment, leaving carriers to reassess their options. SpaceX's Starlink has been generating revenue from internet services in sparsely populated and rural areas, but becoming a true rival to major carriers will require years of work and a terrestrial network. Tower operator Crown Castle, however, surged 11.6 per cent after the report identified it as one of the cellular infrastructure companies SpaceX was in talks with.  Other operators also rose, with American Tower up 4.9 per cent and SBA Communications adding 4.6 per cent.  Shares of SpaceX rose 1.7 per cent.

Oct 23 : PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data. • A PwC global spokesperson said "the affected site does not house client data, sensitive personal data or financial information. Once we learned of this incident we acted promptly to secure the environment and conduct a thorough review." • The incident "does not impact our network or any of our operations," the spokesperson said. • A cyber extortion group called "Everest" claimed responsibility for the data breach in a message posted to its website October 22, according to cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The message included a countdown timer with five days remaining, and a message indicating the data would be released if a deal could not be reached.

Oct 23 : Telecom giants AT&T and T-Mobile are investing to safeguard customer data and network infrastructure from new cybersecurity threats as AI integration ramps up, though fully autonomous networks remain years away, company executives told Reuters. As AI agents automate workflows and data analysis, with declining human intervention, cybersecurity concerns are growing across industries over access to sensitive information and connected software. For telecom operators, which manage vast amounts of customer data and critical communications infrastructure, vulnerabilities in AI systems or third-party software could extend from data breaches to network disruptions. "Yes, we are increasing our investments in how we monitor and react," T-Mobile's Chief Technology Officer John Saw told the Reuters Global Markets Forum. The company simultaneously works with vendors to ensure security holes are closed as soon as possible, he added.

The Bellevue, Washington-based wireless carrier has suffered several data breaches, including incidents in 2021 and 2023, cumulatively impacting over 100 million customer accounts. It has agreed to various settlements with consumers and the Federal Communications Commission involving cybersecurity penalties and investments. AT&T, meanwhile, warned that third-party software providers and AI agents pose cybersecurity risks that extend beyond operators' own networks. "There (are) industry problems, not things that AT&T can solve by itself," CTO Jeremy Legg said, questioning if the open-source community followed comparable security standards. The Texas-based company has deployed AI governance controls such as encryption, multi-factor authentication and human oversight of data access. It is also working to verify whether third-party AI agents seeking access to customer accounts are acting on behalf of legitimate customers, the company said. AI has automated aspects of network management for telecom operators, but handing over entire networks to AI-driven autonomous systems is still "years away," Legg said, as human intervention is still required to solve complex network problems. For instance, AT&T has automated some tasks such as analyzing trouble tickets to identify potential fixes and, in some cases, automatically implementing repairs. T-Mobile, meanwhile, uses AI to automatically adjust cell-site antennas when nearby sites go down to compensate for coverage gaps. During Winter Storm Fern in January, T-Mobile's self-organizing network, or SON, restored coverage to about 66 per cent of customers within an hour and 90 per cent within eight hours, with most customers regaining service before power was restored, Saw said. MUNICH, Germany, Oct 23 : Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing during a training session, the German champions said. The Belgian had been nursing a virus in recent days and had missed some of his team's training sessions. "On Friday, Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during a training session for Bayern’s reserve team," the club said. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage all training and match-related operations."

WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : US President Donald Trump said on Friday that if there was still a problem with access to Starlink communication systems in Ukraine, he would get it straightened out. Trump told reporters at the White House that he had not spoken to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk about the matter but, if access was not fixed, he would speak to him. "If there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out," Trump said. The caps have been in place since October 13 as relations between Kyiv and Washington deteriorated Ukrainian officials said on Friday that speed restrictions on Starlink communication systems in Ukraine remained in place, contradicting Trump's previous statement that the services had been fully restored. "Elon will never do anything wrong. I know him very well. He's a fair person, and you know it's an unusual situation where they're talking to a private company. But he's not going to do anything that's wrong," Trump said.

Oct 23 : England's Ian Poulter is the latest player to leave LIV Golf, saying he will not be part of the proposed 2.0 relaunch as he looks to focus on senior golf and spend more time with family. Poulter's announcement comes days after former British Open champion Louis Oosthuizen said he was moving on from the breakaway circuit, whose future remains uncertain. Former world number one Jon Rahm is also among those quitting LIV, which is fighting to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund said in April it was cutting funding. LIV has secured investment from BC Partners Credit and is set to make a decision this month on whether it winds down or moves forward with a 2.0 model.

"I have decided to not move forward with being part of LIV 2.0," Poulter said in a lengthy post on X. "Needless to say, it was a tough decision and one I thought about and discussed at length with my family and team." The 50-year-old, a five-times Ryder Cup winner, did not win an individual or team title during his time with LIV but boasts 17 professional victories, including three on the PGA Tour. "Ultimately, the opportunity to spend more time at home with my family, reduce international travel, focus on senior golf and have the opportunity to pursue other interests was something that I felt was right for me at this stage of my life and career," Poulter said. He was part of LIV's inaugural event in June 2022 and later became one of the leaders of Majesticks GC alongside Lee Westwood and Henrik Stenson. Poulter was among a group of established stars who accepted lucrative contracts to join the breakaway circuit from the traditional tours and was a vocal defender of the move. “Change is never easy and it's fair to say professional golf has experienced plenty of it over the last few years," Poulter said. "But I've always believed that change can create opportunity and ultimately lead to positive outcomes."

Source: Reuters

JOHANNESBURG, Oct 23 : South Africa's presidency temporarily took its website offline following a PHP warning, presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya told Reuters on Friday, adding there was no indication of a security breach. "While such warnings do not indicate a security breach, they can affect the normal operation of a website," Magwenya said. He added that the website was taken down as a precaution. Governments and businesses worldwide have rushed to secure systems running the PHP programming language after flaws were disclosed, forcing some services offline and triggering millions of hacking attempts in one of the most significant cybersecurity incidents in recent years. PHP underpins a large share of the public web and is widely used by content management systems including WordPress, Drupal and Joomla, giving any critical vulnerability potentially widespread consequences. PHP developers on Wednesday released fixes for the flaws and urged users to update affected systems immediately.

Oct 23 : The firebrand grandson of former Uganda dictator Idi Amin has been disqualified from a major boxing tournament for the second time in a matter of months after a wild punch thrown at an opponent after the bell. Aziz Abdul swung at Egypt's Mohamed Hossen in their men's 90-kilogramme final at the African Boxing Championships in Nairobi and was immediately disqualified and stripped of his silver medal. The blow struck Hossen on the back of the head after he had turned away from Abdul, but the Egyptian was uninjured. The 25-year-old Abdul, who goes by the name of ‘Ringo’, was also disqualified from the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow after he headbutted Damar Thomas from England in the opening round.

WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : Six more companies, including Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit, will not allow their shares to be tokenized on a joint trading platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, according to a regulatory document seen by Reuters.  The new objections, which have not been previously reported, underscore the growing challenges for tokenization, the creation of digital tokens that represent a stock and can be traded on a blockchain similar to cryptocurrencies, despite the US securities regulator recently approving the novel products.  In total, 22 companies have objected, according to the document, which outlines the rules of the OKXICE venture and which companies have objected. It does not say why the companies objected. Sixteen of the companies, including Microsoft and Alphabet, are listed on Nasdaq. The others are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, which ICE owns. Nasdaq has teamed up with Payward, the parent of crypto exchange Kraken, to launch its own tokenized stock platform next year.

A spokesperson for Arm did not immediately provide comment. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo and Intuit declined to comment.  TOKENIZATION ADVOCATES TOUT 24/7 TRADING The cryptocurrency industry has said stock tokenization could revolutionize markets by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly. OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks through their joint venture, but have encountered objections from issuers. OKX and ICE filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month to launch tokenized stocks under the agency's new innovation exemption. The exemption allows platforms that facilitate trading of tokenized stocks to operate without complying with many requirements that apply to traditional stock exchanges.  Under the exemption, platforms must notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their stocks, and cannot proceed if the issuer objects.   Speaking to reporters this week, Andrew Cuomo, co-chairman of the OKXICE joint venture, said given how revolutionary tokenization could be, it was natural for companies to take a "wait and see" approach, CoinDesk reported. While Nasdaq says it welcomes tokenization in principle, it has said such products should be subject to the existing set of rules and investor protections. It has warned that if improperly regulated, tokenization could fragment liquidity and undermine price discovery, among other issues.  "Given the risks we believe issuers must be cautious about their participation," the company warned in a September FAQ.  A Nasdaq spokesperson pointed Reuters to its FAQ. Although many overseas tokenized stocks are marketed like stocks, they rarely offer the same rights, disclosures and protections as traditional equities.  Under the SEC's exemption, tokenized stocks must confer the same rights and privileges as traditional securities, including the ability to receive dividends and exercise voting rights.

Source: Reuters

Oct 23 : Tottenham Hotspur's James Maddison is doubtful for the trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the midfielder scored in his first start in 536 days during the club's first Premier League win of the season, manager Roberto De Zerbi said on Friday. Spurs head to Stamford Bridge on the back of Monday's encouraging 3-1 home victory over Coventry City but have won only once there in the last 41 visits in all competitions. The 29-year-old Maddison, who recently returned from a lengthy injury layoff, marked his return to the starting lineup by opening the scoring against Coventry with a superb strike. "In the first three days (after the Coventry game) Maddison didn't work with us. I don't know if he's ready for tomorrow," De Zerbi told a press conference.

Oct 23 : Fuel cells are gaining traction among US hyperscalers racing to build data centers for the AI boom but struggling with grid constraints to secure quick and reliable power. Energy research firm Rystad Energy projects investments in fuel cells for data centers to rise to about $30 billion by 2030 from $2.8 billion in 2025. WHAT ARE FUEL CELLS? A fuel cell generates electricity through a chemical reaction between a fuel, such as natural gas or hydrogen, and oxygen, converting the fuel's energy directly into electricity rather than burning it.

Bloom Energy operates solid-oxide technology ready for 100 per cent pure hydrogen, while FuelCell Energy uses molten carbonate technology capped at 40 per cent hydrogen blends, even as both systems are fuel-flexible. WHY IS DEMAND GROWING? Data centers require massive amounts of reliable electricity to run computing equipment and cooling systems around the clock. Linking large electricity loads to the US grid can take three to six years, according to Rystad estimates, prodding developers to explore on-site power sources. "We announced our first project with Oracle and delivered power to their Utah site in less than two months," Bloom CEO KR Sridhar said on a post-earnings call on Thursday. "We are achieving the same thing with Nebius in New Jersey. We were able to get planning board approvals for our fuel cells within three months of signing the contract." Rystad predicts that about 40 per cent of projected US data-center capacity in 2030 could pursue dedicated on-site power rather than rely entirely on the grid. Fuel cells also produce lower local emissions than conventional gas-fired generation, as they avoid combustion within the stack. WHICH COMPANIES STAND TO BENEFIT? Bloom's third-quarter revenue surged 138 per cent to $1.24 billion. The company posted net profit of $250.3 million, compared to a year-earlier loss of $23.1 million. It raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion. US cloud computing giant Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 gigawatts (GW) of Bloom fuel-cell systems, of which 1.2 GW has been contracted. FuelCell is also targeting data centers. CEO Jason Few told Reuters that "time to power has really become as important as cost of power." The company expects data centers and related business to account for 75 per cent-85 per cent of its business within two to three years, up from 25 per cent-30 per cent currently. Rystad estimates the industry's order book at roughly 9 GW, including framework agreements involving Oracle, AEP, Equinix and Brookfield. Such agreements do not necessarily represent firm orders for the full stated capacity. CAN THE INDUSTRY SCALE FAST ENOUGH? Rystad expects annual fuel-cell manufacturing capacity to rise to 4 GW by 2030 from about 1.8 GW currently. "For 100 MW-plus projects, the biggest determinants of timeline are typically site readiness, permitting, and supporting infrastructure, not the fuel-cell technology itself," Bloom Chief Commercial Officer Aman Joshi told Reuters. Projects still need gas connections, permits, transformers and switchgear, which can delay deployment. Fuel cells can complement grid power, even as they compete with other on-site generation technologies. Growth depends on whether suppliers can deliver systems at competitive costs and developers can build projects and secure fuel.

Source: Reuters

COPENHAGEN, Oct 23 : Denmark's heavy reliance on digital systems leaves it vulnerable to cyberattacks that could undermine public trust in authorities, the country's resilience minister told Reuters on Friday. Denmark is among the world's most digitalised countries, and confidence in its digital public services is high. Governments and companies worldwide, including in Denmark, this week took websites offline after critical flaws in a widely used programming language triggered millions of hacking attempts. Danish municipal IT company Kombit, for example, said it had shut down several services, including the national school communication platform. Resilience and Preparedness Minister Lisbeth Bech-Nielsen said Denmark's early embrace of digitalisation had delivered major benefits but also increased its exposure to cyber threats.

Utilities, healthcare and financial services all depend heavily on digital infrastructure. Her main concern is public confidence. Even attacks that cause limited disruption can weaken trust in authorities, she said, while the steady stream of reports about cyber incidents "has a very destructive impact on society". "The new normal is that we're going to be attacked on a daily basis, whether it's Russia, whether it's criminal hackers doing it for economic gain or something else," she said. The high level of trust Danes place in public institutions was evident during the COVID-19 pandemic, when strong vaccine uptake helped the country reopen society relatively quickly. Bech-Nielsen said Denmark needed to invest more in its digital infrastructure and reconsider how much critical equipment should be connected to the internet. She pointed to an incident in France in which freezers were remotely controlled, and questioned whether more local, closed systems would offer greater security. "We need to change some things fundamentally in how we arrange the digital infrastructure in Denmark, but it will affect a lot of people and a lot of ways of living, of doing business," she said.

Mourinho seeks Real Madrid turning point in Clasico full of new faces

FAST

Oct 22 : Spain's biggest football fixture arrives on Sunday night at Camp Nou with as many as 14 new faces that could make their Clasico debuts, but the return of Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho to the fixture will attract the most attention of all. Real Madrid and Barcelona both made six signings in the close season, while the Catalan club have promoted two youth academy products to their senior squad, injecting the tie with a fresh crop of players keen to leave their mark on the rivalry. Among them is Brazilian striker Gabriel Jesus, who joined Barcelona from Arsenal in September. "Barcelona against Real Madrid is, without a doubt, amongst the biggest in the world," Jesus told Reuters on Thursday ahead of the first meeting between the two sides this season.

"It really is a dream to play in the Clasico for the first time. I've never made a secret of my desire to one day wear the Barcelona shirt and that goal includes playing in El Clasico." Jesus is no stranger to facing Real Madrid, having scored three times against Los Blancos in four matches for Manchester City. "They were memorable Champions League clashes, including a goal at the Bernabeu," he said. The 29-year-old Jesus grew up 8,797km away in Sao Paulo, and he could line up alongside Xavi Espart, who was born in Barcelona and came through their youth academy. One of nine academy graduates in their squad, Espart highlighted the implications of the match both in the standings and in the rivalry. "The truth is, it’s going to be a war. We will go all out, it’s a Clasico," Espart told DAZN on Thursday. "You always have to give 100 per cent, now we have the chance to extend our lead and we'll fight to the death." Victory for Barcelona would extend the gap in LaLiga between the two teams to nine points, a sizable margin to overcome. Should Real come away with a win, it would not only halve the current six-point gap, but provide a much-needed confidence boost for a side that has lost six of the last seven Clasicos. MOURINHO'S RETURN At the other end of the experience scale to Espart is Mourinho. The 63-year-old is a veteran of 27 matches against Barcelona and 17 Clasicos on the Real bench. Real Madrid President Florentino Perez first appointed Mourinho as manager in 2010 to compete with Pep Guardiola's Barcelona, and he will hope the Portuguese can wrest the LaLiga title back to the Bernabeu for a second time. Mourinho's first spell at Real coincided with arguably the most heated encounters in the modern history of El Clasico, and there will be numerous cameras trained on his every move at Camp Nou on Sunday. The Portuguese manager won just once in his first 10 Clasicos, but went unbeaten in his final five games against Barcelona, recording three victories. Recovering the winning formula against Barcelona may well represent a turning point in Mourinho's second Real Madrid tenure, after two losses in their opening nine LaLiga games and frequent whistles from their own fans during home games.

Source: Reuters

FAST

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 23 : Manchester United manager Michael Carrick mounted an impassioned defence of his leadership on Friday, accepting responsibility for the club's collapse in form and saying he remains convinced he can lead the team out of their current crisis. Carrick's position is under increasing pressure after United extended their winless run to seven matches in all competitions with Wednesday's humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como leaving them 20th in the table with three points. Before taking questions ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, Carrick delivered an emotional opening statement, acknowledging supporters' frustrations and the scale of the challenge facing him. "Recently, we haven't had a good time. I think that's pretty obvious. So I totally accept what we're going through at the moment," he said.

"We had five months of relative success (last season) in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things I was seeing and that we were doing as a team," he said. "We haven't done well enough lately. We've had a spell that we're really not happy with." Carrick described the loss in Italy as one of the most painful nights of his tenure. "Wednesday was a bad night. It was a bad night for a lot of reasons. It hurt a lot," he said. "It obviously hurt me to see us play that way. As I said after the game, it was really unacceptable." The defeat intensified scrutiny of Carrick after captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to question United's tactical approach in his post-match comments. DRESSING ROOMS CRACKS? Asked whether public criticism from players suggested cracks within the dressing room, Carrick rejected any suggestion the squad was split. He also sidestepped questions over Fernandes' future as captain and declined to reveal whether he had held talks with the Portugal midfielder following the defeat. Instead, he stressed that his priority was restoring an identity that has disappeared from the side in recent weeks. "My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show," Carrick said. "We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I'm fully aware of and definitely doing something about." He reserved special mention for United's fans, many of whom travelled to Como only to watch their side suffer the heaviest defeat of his reign. "The supporters are a huge part of this football club. They have to make the effort and the time and money they spend, to feel how we all felt on Wednesday was a tough moment," he said. DEFIANT TONE Despite growing speculation about his future, Carrick struck a defiant tone, saying he remained confident United could rediscover the energy and connection that characterised last season's performances. He took over in January 2026 after the sacking of Ruben Amorim and oversaw a remarkable turnaround, steering United to a top-three finish and Champions League qualification. "For them (the fans) to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year ... is something we need to get back to. We will get back to it. I fully believe that," said Carrick. Former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager Antonio Conte is among the names linked with United's managerial job, although the 57-year-old Italian said on Friday he had not had any negotiations "at an advanced stage" with any club. Carrick acknowledged that United had lost their way but said responsibility rested squarely with him. He ended his opening remarks by saying it was his duty to guide the club back on course, describing his role as "holding the umbrella for me to get wet and everyone else to stay dry". United are 13th in the Premier League standings on seven points, while Bournemouth are a point behind them in 15th.

Source: Reuters
